title: Intrinsic and Extrinsic Semiconductors
notes: **Intrinsic semiconductor:** pure semiconductor material with no significant impurities. Electron-hole pairs are created thermally in equal numbers.
**Extrinsic semiconductor:** doped with impurity atoms to increase conductivity. Doping introduces either extra electrons (n-type) or extra holes (p-type).
**n-type doping:** pentavalent atoms (Group V: P, As, Sb) have five valence electrons. Four bond with silicon, leaving one extra free electron. Electrons are majority carriers.
**p-type doping:** trivalent atoms (Group III: B, Al, Ga) have three valence electrons. They create a hole in the silicon lattice because only three bonds form. Holes are majority carriers.

**Conductivity control:** by controlling the type and amount of doping, semiconductors can be engineered with precise electrical properties, forming the basis of diodes, transistors, and integrated circuits.
